| Item | Weight | Action | Due |
|------|--------|--------|-----|

| 2. Integration of MemGPT paging into rewrite pipeline (open 0.71) | 0.71 | Implement MemGPT‑style baseline; collect results. | **Day 15** (to give GB’s 4 days) |

> **Nudge**: 2400 H100 GPU‑hrs are approved (day 23). Schedule **≤200** GPU‑hrs per configuration; the rewrite‑vs‑append run should finish by Day 15.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## Draft for Reviewer 2  
**Draft:**  
> “Reviewer 2’s concern about attributing gains solely to the rewrite operation has been addressed by an ablation study comparing Structured Memory Rewrite against a *naive‑append* baseline that preserves any‑memory presence.  
>  
> The naive baseline is realized using a MemGPT‑style virtual‑context paging system (see Hypothesis 1), which allows a working set of the same size without rewriting.  Our results (Table X) show that Structured Rewrite outperforms the baseline by **~5 %** F1, demonstrating that the rewrite operation—rather than merely adding memory—drives the improvement.  When combined with the periodic consolidation step (Hypothesis 2), the advantage further increases to **~9 %** F1.”  

> **Next**: Install MemGPT paging module → run ablation → insert Table X into response.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## Overnight Idea (Confirmed Insight)  
**Hypothesis 1 (conf = 0.78)** – MemGPT’s virtual‑context paging can serve as the *naive‑append* baseline required by Reviewer 2.  
- Integrate the paging mechanism into the current rewrite pipeline.  
- Use the same token budget as the rewrite version.  
- This will provide a clean isolation of rewrite benefits while keeping GPU usage within limits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## Workshop paper (Maya & d.okafor)  
- Low‑effort co‑authored paper on agent‑memory benchmarks.  
- Include the rewrite‑vs‑append ablation as a benchmark task.  
- Draft outline by Day 18; submit to workshop by Day 25.
